name: Huntersville
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Huntersville, NC 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Huntersville, NC: Birkdale on Ice, Breakfast with Santa, Wintersville, the Lake Norman boat parade, Raptor Tales and more.
lede: Huntersville celebrates Christmas at Birkdale Village, at a children's museum that turns into Wintersville, and on Lake Norman, where decorated boats parade in the evening.
celebrates: Birkdale Village sets the tone with its outdoor ice rink, Birkdale on Ice, and a Breakfast with Santa at Red Rocks Cafe that raises money for Operation Wakesurf. Discovery Place Kids on Gilead Road becomes Wintersville, with sock skating and indoor snowballs, and adds Sundays with Santa. Hugh Torance House and Store holds a Holiday Living History Day, Carolina Raptor Center tells a Christmas story with its birds of prey, and the town joins the Lake Norman Lighted Christmas Boat Parade. The town also holds a tree lighting with Holidays in Huntersville.
lastyear: The Lake Norman Lighted Christmas Boat Parade is in its eighth year in 2026, so the 2025 parade was the seventh annual, with boats passing Blythe Landing, Ramsey Creek Park and The Peninsula Yacht Club and a finale at the Duke Energy Explorium, according to the Visit Lake Norman listing. Birkdale Village has listed Birkdale on Ice as a seasonal attraction, and its 2026 season starts on November 21.
facts: Hugh Torance House and Store sits at 8231 Gilead Road, and its Holiday Living History Day features a colonial cooking demonstration, carolers and a visit to the historic store. Discovery Place Kids Huntersville is at 105 Gilead Road and fills its December days with puppet shows, science shows, storytime and a dance party. Birkdale on Ice is listed at 8712 Lindholm Drive, Suite 206, and its skating sessions last 75 minutes.
trains: There is no train ride in Huntersville itself. The closest family train outing we have verified is the North Carolina Transportation Museum in Spencer, in Rowan County, which offers 25-minute train rides and lists seasonal events including The Polar Express. Closer to home, the Polar Express Movie Screening at Romare Bearden Park in Uptown Charlotte on December 12 is a free way to enjoy the story.
train_links: Admission from $10, or $20 with a 25-minute train ride, at the old Spencer Shops in Rowan County; the museum lists seasonal events including The Polar Express.
traditions: An outdoor ice rink at Birkdale Village with 75-minute skating sessions from November 21 to January 10.
A buffet breakfast at Red Rocks Cafe with Santa, Elsa and Anna, raising money for Operation Wakesurf.
Discovery Place Kids turns into a winter play space with sock skating, indoor snowballs and science shows.
Lake Norman Lighted Christmas Boat Parade
Decorated boats pass Blythe Landing and Ramsey Creek Park, with toy donations collected for Toys for Little Smiles.
A colonial cooking demonstration and carolers at the Hugh Torance House and Store.
kidfact: Wintersville at Discovery Place Kids includes ice block building, and the museum's holiday meet and greet with Santa is held on three Sundays in December.
faq: What Christmas events can kids enjoy in Huntersville?

Families can skate at Birkdale on Ice, eat Breakfast with Santa at Birkdale Village, play in Wintersville at Discovery Place Kids, watch the Lake Norman boat parade, visit the Hugh Torance House and Store, or hear Raptor Tales at Carolina Raptor Center. Each has its own date and ticket rules on its page.
Where can children meet Santa in Huntersville?
Birkdale Village hosts Breakfast with Santa and a seasonal Santa visit, and Discovery Place Kids holds Sundays with Santa. Pricing differs, so open each event page for the details the host lists.
Is there an ice rink in Huntersville?
Yes. Birkdale on Ice is the outdoor rink at Birkdale Village. It is listed at $18 for a 75-minute session and is open from November 21, 2026 to January 10, 2027.
Can we see Christmas lights on the water?
Yes. The Lake Norman Lighted Christmas Boat Parade features decorated boats along the Huntersville shoreline, and watching from shore is free.
Are there free Christmas events in Huntersville?
Yes. The Huntersville tree lighting, the St. Mark's holiday market, the Hugh Torance House living history day, the boat parade and several library programs are listed as free.
